title: I'm making an interactive story, not sure if that's technically a game or not, and could use some advice
author: BlitzAce71
selftext:
I've always wanted to create a time loop story. It's one of my favorite genres of fiction and I've tried writing just the straight story versions before but never really liked the results. Well, I've also been using Claude a bunch for other projects and decided to take a crack at a little interactive story, sort of a choose-your-own-adventure style with art and choices and sound effects, and while I am pretty tickled with how far it's come in only a week of prompting with Claude, I don't really know if this is something worth sharing with others or if it was just a fun way to spend my time for a few days. It certainly has the feel of an AI project (to me), and I'm not going to pretend that this is some groundbreaking story idea or anything like that, but I'm just wondering if you guys think this is decent or shit, and what you might suggest changing or any technical pointers you might have. Thanks :)

  
[https://claude.ai/artifact/EyDhuFZbWzNwtEy73kgGo3](https://claude.ai/artifact/EyDhuFZbWzNwtEy73kgGo3)

comments.author: ericoinen
comments.body: time loops are fun for this. the part i'd check first is whether anything the player learns carries into the next loop, like a name or a door code from loop two that opens a new choice in loop four. couldn't tell from the post whether yours does that already

replies.author: BlitzAce71
replies.body: Good advice, but it does, Claude built a logic checker and analyzed the different paths to look for inconsistencies. I've play tested a bunch and it's been a few days since I've found a plot hole, but I'm still on the lookout for them :)

comments.author: Ferniclestix
comments.body:
Hi, I write fiction as a hobby myself so i got a little knowledge about such things. I've also tried integrating some use of AI to polish my own works.

My advice is this, never have the AI write the story for you. most people can spot AI written stuff a mile off.  short passages usually people dont really notice.  you will however see a few patterns after you have used ai for a bit, they tend to do the same kind of things.  


In choose your own adventures, imo, never tell the reader they made an action when they werent given the choice.  cos that feels like you are on rails.

secondly, you gotta grab the reader in the first paragraph or two and make them want to keep reading, if the start is boring you will lose them very quickly, so the starts super important, not just in games but in writing.

  
on your game. mmm... clicking continue repeatedly is annoying.  either make an option to just scroll or disable the clickfest.  clicks arent engagement or interactivity. its a task the reader must perform and it gates progress that would be much faster by letting them read through. 

pauses should be used only in important moments, like when you want to grab the readers attention such as at a crisis point, just before a scene change or an explosion or whatever. 

everything the reader/player experiences is a moment of time they are giving you to show them something awesome. so any point where you interrupt it or  do something as a matter of course, ask yourself, is that thing there for a reason or is it there just because ive always put the thing there.

  
just my opinion though.  seems ok, it didn't really drag me in in those first frew screens tho so i just started clicking rapidly through everything, steam punks never really been my scene tho. more an isekai, grimdark survival type.  

anyway, hope the critique helps you out a bit. not ment to be harsh or anything. take what you want and ignore what you dont.

replies.author: BlitzAce71
replies.body: Very nice of you to take the time, thanks for the feedback! ♥️

comments.author: arcarsenal986
comments.body:
If you find a nice hook, people will read it, whether it's interactive or not. I draft very quick, I do let AI do a bit of work, and then I edit it.

https://i.redd.it/51k600rnla0i1.png

If you keep control, it's not going to go crazy and be any more repetitive than a human writer.  
For example, I post on some story sharing websites.

Here's how I do it, I keep plugging away, then I go back, refine my drafting skills, reread it and add more depth, tighten dialogue. On one particular pass, I ended up taking about 2-3 weeks and adding another 20 chapters to the beginning. I also upped my word count.

Its all in tweaking to get the desired outcome. It might seem great to you at first, but you'll quickly realize that you're not happy with it, and start over. Do not be afraid to shelf material. I've shelved nearly 250 chapters over the last 2 years.

replies.author: BlitzAce71
replies.body: Thanks! Took a while to get the art the way I liked it, but once I did I thought it came together nicely as well :)

comments.author: Bavariasnaps
comments.body: visually everything feels very thight in closed spaces. I would prefer to see the wide landscape of the sky being on upper decks showing the sunset over the clouds, looking down cities. You missed a lot of chances here. The scenery kind of makes sense and there is a certain vibe but its not super interesting or stunning. And for me the ratio text vs images is off. Way to much text compared to visual striking images. Also some task where you click at certain stuff and maybe solve a riddle is missing.  And yeah without progress bar it feels like an infinite adventure that will never end.

comments.author: Ferniclestix
comments.body:
My advice is that for games you want to have a good grasp of the hemmingway iceberg style of writing.  it can really help because its all about keeping things simple whilst sitting upon a layer of deep lore.  through simple actions and dialog we expose tiny fractions of the deeper iceberg.

the simplicity of the writing keeps the reader engaged while the bedrock of lore keeps the story well grounded in a plausible reality. 

Heres a look at my current wip project lol.  written by my own terrible dyslexic hand XD



Chronicle of Torment  
Prologue.

It never ceases to amaze me how little makes a man. A memory here, a tragedy there. A small triumph. Each a tiny fragment of the whole lifetime, yet somehow, that's you, me, anyone. Ask them to retell their life story and it's a bare few scenes, all held in a tangle of our own opinions of our past actions.

We are, in effect, a fiction crafted from a few memories—a critique upon barely remembered actions taken and things said.

It surprised me to learn that most of what we think is not, in fact, dictated by conscious acts. It is, in fact, us explaining our body's own seemingly spontaneous acts. Somehow, with all this said, my past and yours both make us a person.

This might not seem relevant to you, traveller—not yet, anyway. But here I am, trying to weave those separate pasts, fragmented moments, and actions into a structure that not only explains who I am but how I got here.

I suppose the question is, would you have done the same as I?

And if so, does that damn the both of us?

https://i.redd.it/lkejhf0mtl0i1.jpeg

Chapter 1: The Wall

I still remember how it began, the first day of Torment.

It was instant. There I was. Burning heat surrounded me, weighing down upon me like a wool blanket on a hot summer's day. Dry air worked its way into my lungs, stinging my cracked lips.

My sight was cloudy, gritty, and I blinked rapidly as I tried to see anything. Slowly, a red-tinged darkness resolved around me. It didn't make sense, but I pushed it aside as I struggled to move. The ground was nearly as warm as the searing air, its smooth surface unforgiving beneath me.

My struggles amounted to little; pushing simply made my shaking arms collapse. The bone-deep ache not allowing me more than a newborn's strength. That pain seemed to centre on every joint and right behind my eyes. Every exertion making my muscles twitch and cramp painfully. My breath came in panting gasps as my heart raced uncontrollably.

What... what's happening? What the f\*k? I'd been... somewhere. It was so hard to think. There had been dark and time—lots of time. I shuddered as I sucked painfully at the dry air. My mouth felt gummy and I could not work up the saliva to spit the acidic taste from my mouth.

The world around me seemed to fade into fogginess. It felt like I was falling as a deep, black redness swirled about me, pain ripping into me. A dizzy darkness fell.



This bit of writing is designed to suck you in two ways,  the prolog slaps you in the face with a mystery and a question to be answered..   
the second part leaves you wanting to know whats next.   not perfect its a first draft.    but maybe it presents some ideas.
